title: Predicting antioxidant activity of wood vinegar using color and spectrophotometric parameters
author: Petchpoung, Soiklom, et al.

steps.title: Dilute wood vinegar sample
steps.instruction: Dilute the wood vinegar with an appropriate solvent so that the resulting absorbance falls within the range of 0.1–1.0 at the wavelengths 280, 420, 430, 510, 520, 530, 610 and 620 nm.

steps.title: Measure CIELAB color parameters
steps.instruction: Using a HunterLab Ultrascan Pro colorimeter (USA) set to illuminant D65, 10° observer and a 10 mm path‑length cell, record the CIELAB values L*, a* and b* of the diluted wood‑vinegar sample.

steps.title: Record UV‑Vis absorbance spectra
steps.instruction: Place the diluted sample in a 10 mm path‑length cell of a Shimadzu UV‑1800 spectrophotometer (Japan) and measure the absorbance at 280, 420, 430, 510, 520, 530, 610 and 620 nm.

steps.title: Compute EBC color units
steps.instruction: Multiply the absorbance measured at 430 nm by 25 and by the dilution factor; the product is the EBC color value.

steps.title: Compute IOB color units
steps.instruction: Multiply the absorbance measured at 530 nm by 1,000 and by the dilution factor; the product is the IOB color value.

steps.title: Calculate wine color intensity
steps.instruction: Add the absorbance values (each multiplied by the dilution factor) at 420 nm, 520 nm and 620 nm; the sum is the color intensity (CI).

steps.title: Determine Linner Hue index
steps.instruction: Compute HL = 10 log10[(A510 × dilution factor) / (A610 × dilution factor)], where A510 and A610 are the absorbances at 510 nm and 610 nm, respectively.

steps.title: Calculate polyphenol index I280
steps.instruction: Multiply the absorbance measured at 280 nm by the dilution factor; the result is the UV absorbance polyphenol index (I280).
